title: Uniform Inference on Individual Treatment-Effect Distributions with Estimated Factors
banked_reason: D0.5 FINAL: achieved tier subfield below required field floor; the repaired note is mathematically sound with math and rubric PASS and no findings, but is not salvageable to field within the same bounded scope.
gap_reasons: The advertised matching frontier is narrower than a full minimax equivalence: achievability is not shown uniformly over the lower-bound class, and the quantile converse applies only to intervals induced by honest CDF bands rather than arbitrary honest quantile procedures.

The known-rank, homoskedastic Gaussian model, extensive sample splitting, strong-block conditions, and absence of the simulations the note itself calls required substantially limit the projected leading-journal score.

[D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 7.1 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'subfield'. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]
proof_attempt_summary: The run derived a corrected split-sample factor-panel estimator, a whole-line latent-effect ECDF limit, feasible CDF and central-quantile bands, and two Gaussian-subexperiment width lower bounds. A bounded repair cleared every math and rubric finding, including score-family regularity, total inverse/fallback specification, kernel normalization, comparator coverage, and conservative-honesty wording. The result remained subfield because its achievability and quantile converse do not establish the advertised full minimax frontier and the model scope is too narrow to clear the fixed field floor.
tldr: Can one conduct fully feasible, whole-line inference on a latent treatment-effect distribution when counterfactual factors are estimated from controls and their common error remains first order? In a known-fixed-rank Gaussian panel with a specified regular conditional effect law on compact loading support, independent training and calibration blocks permit an observable pre-inversion noise-Gram correction. The project seeks a separable bridge-plus-loading-weighted-Gaussian ECDF limit, an explicitly measurable monotone-clipped multiplier band and its central-quantile inversion, and a Gaussian subexperiment lower bound showing that the matching \(N_1^{-1/2}+(N_0q)^{-1/2}\) width is unavoidable even when \(N_1/(N_0q)\) does not vanish.
gap: The verified literature separates noisy-iid-draw ECDF theory from factor-panel inference for entries, factors, loadings, and averages. It does not supply a located theorem for a nonsmooth latent-effect ECDF with persistent shared control-estimation uncertainty and fully observable nuisance correction.
fill: Establish the corrected estimator's uniform stochastic expansion relative to the chosen conditional-density version, estimate both the individual-noise bias and finite-rank common covariance, prove validity of the explicit countably measurable monotone-clipped CDF band and quantile inversion, and use two stated Gaussian local alternatives to match the two leading width orders.
